key_insight: TRACE improves training for long-horizon agents by assigning reward at the turn level instead of relying only on the final outcome. This gives credit to useful intermediate actions even when the overall rollout fails.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the credit assignment problem in multi-turn tool-using agents, where long trajectories make outcome-only rewards sparse, noisy, and misleading.
method: Estimate credit at each turn rather than only at the end of the trajectory.
Use reward assignment to identify which intermediate actions contributed to progress toward the goal.
Train agents with denser supervision so useful steps are reinforced even in failed rollouts.
impact: This can make post-training more stable and effective for agents that perform many tool calls or reasoning steps. For practitioners, it offers a way to learn from partially successful trajectories instead of wasting informative intermediate behavior.
visual_elements: A long agent trajectory split into turns, with color-coded positive/negative credit per step.
A comparison chart showing outcome-only reward vs. turn-level reward across long horizons.
An icon sequence for tool use, intermediate progress, and final answer.
A simple credit assignment flow diagram from rollout to per-turn reward estimation.
paper_title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
paper_authors: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Tao Ge, Hao Cheng
